prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which established the incretin axis as a therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B006 first, but agreement in ranking is not the argument; the argument is the discovery itself. Holst established GLP-1 as the principal incretin and described its secretion and actions in humans, Mojsov identified and synthesised the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker defined receptor biology, tissue actions and the translational concept. This is a discernible change in medicine: a mechanism understood in physiology became a drug class that changed outcomes in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit shown in large randomized trials. Decades of independent confirmation make the discovery mature, and recognition is timely.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Credit is spread across several groups, Habener and others are not among the credited names, and any three-person cap leaves out important contributors. My trio rewards the physiology and the identification of the active peptide, and it omits Knudsen, whose engineering of long-acting acylated analogues made the drug class clinically real. There is also a risk that the prize is read as endorsing a commercial product, and long-term safety data are still accumulating.

responses.point: Svenningsson proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen so that the prize spans physiology and translation, while acknowledging that Mojsov's contribution is hard to leave out.
responses.response: I understand the wish to span bench and bedside, but I disagree on the third name. Nobel recognition is for a discovery, and here the discovery is the physiology and identification of the active peptide. Knudsen's work is excellent drug development, built on that knowledge. Taking Mojsov out to include her would put the translation ahead of a necessary link in the discovery chain. I would reconsider if the committee wished to frame the prize as therapy development, but then the citation and the credit logic would need to change.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks CAR-T second and sees Knudsen's long-acting analogues as what made the drug class, while treating Mojsov's contribution as credited but secondary.
responses.response: I agree that the analogues made the class, but this does not by itself make Knudsen a co-discoverer of the incretin axis. I also hold that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active form is the step that made the biology interpretable. On CAR-T, I rank it lower than you do, mostly because of the Eshhar, Rosenberg, June and Sadelain priority question, which I do not think a three-name trio resolves cleanly. If B006 is settled, this is a candidate to take up next, but only if the attribution holds.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks cGAS-STING third on the strength of its clean mechanism and relevance to autoimmunity, while noting that therapeutic translation has so far been disappointing.
responses.response: I share your view that the mechanism is clean, with Chen on cGAS and cGAMP and Barber on STING. But you yourself note that clinical translation has been disappointing, and I would therefore treat the pathway as somewhat early. Mechanism alone can carry a prize, as the UPR shows, but the UPR has two decades of stability and compact attribution, whereas for cGAS-STING I would want clinical or disease-causation evidence to mature further. That is why I would put B039 ahead of B028 as the alternative.

responses.point: Linnarsson favours the physiology-centred triplet of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B006 and ranks the UPR second, with CAR-T third.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the logic of rewarding physiology over drug design. I would qualify one point: the committee should state openly that this choice leaves out Knudsen and Habener, so that the citation is worded for the physiology and the identification of the active peptide, and does not claim the whole therapeutic chain.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept omitting Knudsen and Habener, and how the citation should be worded to reflect that choice.
Whether the early priority claims for identification of GLP-1(7-36) are fairly captured by the credited names.
Whether a second prize part (for example the UPR) should be paired with B006 or kept for a later year, since the three-person cap would then force removing one of the GLP-1 laureates.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B006, B039, B037 or B004. My documented connections (a nuclear-receptor collaboration with Ronald Evans, work with Johan Ericson, and co-authorship with colleagues on this committee) do not involve any shortlisted candidate or its credited names.
